title: Control Consistency Losses for Diffusion Bridges
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: The target object is the unique intersection of two constraint sets, one satisfied by construction and the other enforced by a loss.
layout: 1 panel, two overlapping circles, Venn diagram, colored labels beneath each circle
description: A two-circle Venn diagram on a white background. The left circle is light blue and labeled in bold blue 'Bridges (3) from x_0 to x_T'. The right circle is light pink and labeled in bold dark red 'Processes satisfying self-consistency'. The overlap is a muted mauve region labeled in large bold black 'Diffusion Bridge', which is where the eye lands first. Below the circles are two captions. In blue, under the left circle: 'Enforced by construction'. In dark red, under the right circle: 'Enforced by self-consistency loss'. Blue and red are used consistently for the circles, labels and captions. The only math notation is the x_0 and x_T subscripts. The figure argues that the diffusion bridge is the unique process satisfying both conditions.

abstract: Simulating the conditioned dynamics of diffusion processes, given their initial and terminal states, is an important but challenging problem in the sciences. The difficulty is particularly pronounced for rare events, for which the unconditioned dynamics rarely reach the terminal state. In this work, we propose a novel approach for learning diffusion bridges based on a self-consistency property of the optimal control. The resulting algorithm learns the conditioned dynamics in an iterative online manner, and exhibits strong performance in a range of empirical settings without requiring differentiation through simulated trajectories. Beyond the diffusion bridge setting, we draw connections between our self-consistency framework and recent advances in the wider stochastic optimal control literature.
